source.text: ה֚וֹי הַשַּׁאֲנַנִּ֣ים בְּצִיּ֔וֹן וְהַבֹּטְחִ֖ים בְּהַ֣ר שֹׁמְר֑וֹן נְקֻבֵי֙ רֵאשִׁ֣ית הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וּבָ֥אוּ לָהֶ֖ם בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Woe [to] those at ease in Zion, and those who trust in [the] mountain of Samaria, the notable [men] of [the] first of the nations, and to them comes the house of Israel!

en.L: Woe, those at ease in Zion, \q and those who feel secure on the mountain of Samaria, \q the notable men of the first of the nations, \q to whom the house of Israel comes!
en.B: Woe to the complacent in Zion, \q and to those who feel secure on the mountain of Samaria, \q the notable leaders of the foremost nation, \q to whom the house of Israel comes!
en.R: How terrible it will be for you who live comfortably in Zion, \q and for you who feel safe on the hill of Samaria! \q You are the important leaders of the greatest nation, \q and the people of Israel come to you for help.

es.L: ¡Ay de los que están tranquilos en Sion, \q y de los que se sienten seguros en el monte de Samaria, \q los notables de la primera de las naciones, \q a quienes acude la casa de Israel!
es.B: ¡Ay de los despreocupados de Sion \q y de los que se sienten seguros en el monte de Samaria, \q los dirigentes notables de la nación más importante, \q a quienes acude la casa de Israel!
es.R: ¡Qué terrible será para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, que {{plural_you:viven|vivís}} cómodamente en Sion, \q y para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, que se {{plural_you:sienten|sentís}} seguros en el monte de Samaria! \q {{plural_you:Son|Sois}} los dirigentes importantes de la nación más grande, \q y el pueblo de Israel acude a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} en busca de ayuda.

fr.L: Malheur, ceux qui sont tranquilles dans Sion, \q et ceux qui se sentent en sécurité sur la montagne de Samarie, \q les notables de la première des nations, \q auprès de qui vient la maison d’Israël !
fr.B: Malheur à ceux qui vivent insouciants dans Sion, \q et à ceux qui se sentent en sécurité sur la montagne de Samarie, \q les chefs en vue de la première des nations, \q auprès de qui vient la maison d’Israël !
fr.R: Quel malheur pour vous qui vivez dans le confort à Sion, \q et pour vous qui vous sentez en sécurité sur la colline de Samarie ! \q Vous êtes les chefs importants de la plus grande des nations, \q et le peuple d’Israël vient vous demander de l’aide.

sw.L: Ole, wale wanaostarehe katika Sayuni, \q na wale wanaojiona salama juu ya mlima wa Samaria, \q watu mashuhuri wa taifa lililo la kwanza kati ya mataifa, \q ambao nyumba ya Israeli huwaendea!
sw.B: Ole wao walioridhika katika Sayuni, \q na wale wanaojiona salama juu ya mlima wa Samaria, \q viongozi mashuhuri wa taifa lililo bora kuliko yote, \q ambao nyumba ya Israeli huwaendea!
sw.R: Itakuwa vibaya sana kwenu ninyi mnaoishi kwa starehe katika Sayuni, \q na kwenu ninyi mnaojiona salama juu ya kilima cha Samaria! \q Ninyi ni viongozi wakuu wa taifa lililo kubwa kuliko yote, \q na watu wa Israeli huja kwenu kuomba msaada.

decisions.choice: Zion and Samaria: the capitals of Judah and Israel
decisions.reason: Zion is Jerusalem, the capital of Judah; the hill of Samaria was the capital of the northern kingdom (3:9; 4:1). Amos speaks mostly to the north, but here the leaders of both kingdoms are named.

decisions.choice: at ease ... secure: careless confidence
decisions.reason: The first word means untroubled or complacent (Isaiah 32:9, 11); the second means trusting, feeling safe. These leaders feel safe because of their walls and their wealth, and do not see the danger.

decisions.choice: the first of the nations: Israel's pride in itself
decisions.reason: The leaders are 'the notable men of the first of the nations', the chief men of what they took to be the greatest nation. In verse 6 they use 'the first' (the finest) of the oils, and in verse 7 they will be the first to go into exile, at the head of the captives. The repeated word is irony.

decisions.choice: to whom the house of Israel comes: the leaders whom the people consult
decisions.reason: The people come to these men for judgment and help. They are responsible for the nation, and they have failed it.

decisions.choice: Woe, (L); Woe to (B); How terrible it will be for (R); come to you for help (R)
decisions.reason: Hoy follows Isaiah's wording at each level, as in 5:18. Readable says why the people come to the leaders (m4), and addresses them as 'you', which the Hebrew does from verse 2 on.

source.text: עִבְר֤וּ כַֽלְנֵה֙ וּרְא֔וּ וּלְכ֥וּ מִשָּׁ֖ם חֲמַ֣ת רַבָּ֑ה וּרְד֣וּ גַת־פְּלִשְׁתּ֗יםהֲטוֹבִים֙ מִן־הַמַּמְלָכ֣וֹת הָאֵ֔לֶּה אִם־רַ֥ב גְּבוּלָ֖ם מִגְּבֻלְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Cross over [to] Calneh and see, and go from there [to] Hamath [the] great, and go down [to] Gath of [the] Philistines. [Are they] better than these kingdoms? Or [is] their territory greater than your territory?

en.L: Cross over to Calneh and see, \q and go from there to Hamath the great; \q and go down to Gath of the Philistines. Are [those cities] better than these kingdoms? \q Or [is] their territory greater than your territory?
en.B: Go over to Calneh and look; \q go on from there to Hamath the great, \q then go down to Philistine Gath. Are those cities better than your kingdoms? \q Is their land larger than yours?
en.R: Go and look at the city of Calneh. \q Then go to the great city of Hamath, \q and go down to Gath, the city of the Philistines. Are they any better than your kingdoms? \q Is their land bigger than yours?

es.L: {{plural_you:Pasen|Pasad}} a Calne y {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}, \q y de allí {{plural_you:vayan|id}} a Hamat la grande; \q y {{plural_you:bajen|bajad}} a Gat de los filisteos. ¿Son [esas ciudades] mejores que estos reinos? \q ¿O [es] su territorio mayor que {{plural_you:su territorio|vuestro territorio}}?
es.B: {{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a Calne y {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}; \q de allí {{plural_you:sigan|seguid}} hasta Hamat la grande, \q y luego {{plural_you:bajen|bajad}} a Gat de los filisteos. ¿Son esas ciudades mejores que {{plural_you:sus reinos|vuestros reinos}}? \q ¿Es su tierra más grande que la {{plural_you:suya|vuestra}}?
es.R: {{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a ver la ciudad de Calne. \q Luego {{plural_you:vayan|id}} a la gran ciudad de Hamat, \q y {{plural_you:bajen|bajad}} a Gat, la ciudad de los filisteos. ¿Son mejores que {{plural_you:sus reinos|vuestros reinos}}? \q ¿Es su tierra más grande que la {{plural_you:suya|vuestra}}?

fr.L: Passez à Calné et voyez, \q et allez de là à Hamath la grande ; \q et descendez à Gath des Philistins. [Ces villes] sont-elles meilleures que ces royaumes-ci ? \q Ou leur territoire [est-il] plus grand que votre territoire ?
fr.B: Passez à Calné et regardez ; \q allez de là jusqu’à Hamath la grande, \q puis descendez à Gath, chez les Philistins. Ces villes valent-elles mieux que vos royaumes ? \q Leur pays est-il plus grand que le vôtre ?
fr.R: Allez voir la ville de Calné. \q Ensuite, allez à la grande ville de Hamath, \q et descendez à Gath, la ville des Philistins. Sont-elles meilleures que vos royaumes ? \q Leur pays est-il plus grand que le vôtre ?

sw.L: Vukeni mwende Kalne mkaone, \q na kutoka huko nendeni Hamathi ule mkuu; \q kisha shukeni Gathi ya Wafilisti. Je, [miji hiyo] ni bora kuliko falme hizi? \q Au nchi yao ni kubwa kuliko nchi yenu?
sw.B: Vukeni mwende Kalne mkatazame; \q kutoka huko nendeni Hamathi ule mkuu, \q kisha shukeni Gathi ya Wafilisti. Je, miji hiyo ni bora kuliko falme zenu? \q Je, nchi yao ni kubwa kuliko yenu?
sw.R: Nendeni mkauone mji wa Kalne. \q Kisha nendeni mpaka mji mkubwa wa Hamathi, \q na mshuke mpaka Gathi, mji wa Wafilisti. Je, miji hiyo ni bora kuliko falme zenu? \q Je, nchi yao ni kubwa kuliko yenu?

decisions.choice: Calneh, Hamath, Gath: city-states to the north and to the south-west
decisions.reason: Calneh and Hamath were cities of northern Syria, and Gath was one of the five cities of the Philistines. The Assyrians captured Calneh and Hamath in the 730s and 720s BC. Gath had been taken by Hazael of Aram (2 Kings 12:18) and later by Uzziah of Judah (2 Chronicles 26:6). If the Syrian cities had already fallen when Amos spoke, he is pointing to them as a warning; if not, he is pointing to what was coming. The text does not say which.

decisions.choice: Are they better ...?: those kingdoms were no greater than Israel and Judah, and they fell
alternatives: Are you better than these kingdoms? (with a small change to the Hebrew)
the leaders' boast: no kingdom is better than ours
decisions.reason: The questions expect the answer 'no'. 'These kingdoms' are probably Israel and Judah, the kingdoms of verse 1. The cities named were no better and no larger, and they have fallen or will fall, so Israel's leaders have no reason to feel secure. Some change the Hebrew slightly to read 'Are you better than these kingdoms?', with the same point. Others take the verse as the leaders' own boast: 'Go and see: no kingdom is better than ours.' The Hebrew is translated as it stands.

decisions.choice: those cities (L, B); your kingdoms (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say who 'they' are, and Balanced and Readable say whose kingdoms 'these kingdoms' are (m2). Readable adds 'the city of' so that readers know that the names are cities.

source.text: הַֽמְנַדִּ֖ים לְי֣וֹם רָ֑ע וַתַּגִּישׁ֖וּן שֶׁ֥בֶת חָמָֽס׃

records.literal_gloss: Those who push away to a day of evil, and you bring near a seat of violence.

en.L: [You] who push away the day of disaster, \q and bring near the seat of violence!
en.B: You put off the day of disaster, \q yet you bring near the reign of violence.
en.R: You think the day of disaster is still far away, \q but you are bringing a time of violence closer by what you do.

es.L: ¡{{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}}, que {{plural_you:alejan|alejáis}} el día de la desgracia, \q y {{plural_you:acercan|acercáis}} el trono de la violencia!
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes alejan|Vosotros alejáis}} el día de la desgracia, \q pero {{plural_you:acercan|acercáis}} el reinado de la violencia.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes creen|Vosotros creéis}} que el día de la desgracia todavía está lejos, \q pero con lo que {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} {{plural_you:están acercando|estáis acercando}} un tiempo de violencia.

fr.L: [Vous] qui repoussez le jour du malheur, \q et faites approcher le règne de la violence !
fr.B: Vous repoussez à plus tard le jour du malheur, \q et pourtant vous faites approcher le règne de la violence.
fr.R: Vous croyez que le jour du malheur est encore loin, \q mais par ce que vous faites, vous rapprochez un temps de violence.

sw.L: [Ninyi] mnaoisukumia mbali siku ya maafa, \q na kukisogeza karibu kiti cha udhalimu!
sw.B: Mnaiahirisha siku ya maafa, \q lakini mnausogeza karibu utawala wa udhalimu.
sw.R: Mnadhani siku ya maafa bado iko mbali, \q lakini kwa matendo yenu mnaleta karibu wakati wa udhalimu.

decisions.choice: push away the day of disaster: refuse to think that disaster will come
decisions.reason: They tell themselves that the evil day is far off (compare 9:10; Ezekiel 12:27). The 'day' is the day of the LORD's judgment (5:18-20).

decisions.choice: bring near the seat of violence: hasten a rule of violence
alternatives: the 'sabbath' (shabbat) of violence, with a small change of the Hebrew
decisions.reason: Shevet is a seat or a sitting, often a throne. By their own violent rule the leaders hasten the very day they want to keep far off, and with it the violence of an enemy who will rule over them. The phrase is short, and either side of it may be meant: their own reign of violence, or the enemy's.

decisions.choice: think ... is still far away; by what you do (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (m1) and says how the leaders bring the violence near (m2).

source.text: הַשֹּֽׁכְבִים֙ עַל־מִטּ֣וֹת שֵׁ֔ן וּסְרֻחִ֖ים עַל־עַרְשׂוֹתָ֑ם וְאֹכְלִ֤ים כָּרִים֙ מִצֹּ֔אן וַעֲגָלִ֖ים מִתּ֥וֹךְ מַרְבֵּֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: Those who lie on beds of ivory and sprawl on their couches, and eat lambs from [the] flock and calves from [the] midst of [the] stall,

en.L: Those who lie on beds of ivory \q and sprawl on their couches, \q and eat lambs from the flock \q and calves from the midst of the stall,
en.B: They lie on beds inlaid with ivory \q and sprawl on their couches; \q they eat lambs from the flock \q and calves fattened in the stall.
en.R: They lie on beds decorated with ivory \q and lounge on their couches. \q They eat lambs from the flock \q and calves fattened in the stall.

es.L: Los que se acuestan en camas de marfil \q y se tienden sobre sus divanes, \q y comen corderos del rebaño \q y becerros de en medio del establo,
es.B: Se acuestan en camas con incrustaciones de marfil \q y se tienden sobre sus divanes; \q comen corderos del rebaño \q y becerros engordados en el establo.
es.R: Se acuestan en camas adornadas con marfil \q y se recuestan en sus divanes. \q Comen corderos del rebaño \q y becerros engordados en el establo.

fr.L: Ceux qui se couchent sur des lits d’ivoire \q et s’étalent sur leurs divans, \q et mangent les agneaux du troupeau \q et les veaux pris au milieu de l’étable,
fr.B: Ils se couchent sur des lits incrustés d’ivoire \q et s’étalent sur leurs divans ; \q ils mangent les agneaux du troupeau \q et les veaux engraissés à l’étable.
fr.R: Ils se couchent sur des lits décorés d’ivoire \q et se prélassent sur leurs divans. \q Ils mangent les agneaux du troupeau \q et les veaux engraissés à l’étable.

sw.L: Wale wanaolala juu ya vitanda vya pembe za ndovu \q na kujinyoosha juu ya makochi yao, \q na kula wana-kondoo kutoka kundini \q na ndama kutoka katikati ya zizi,
sw.B: Wanalala juu ya vitanda vilivyonakshiwa kwa pembe za ndovu \q na kujinyoosha juu ya makochi yao; \q wanakula wana-kondoo kutoka kundini \q na ndama walionenepeshwa zizini.
sw.R: Wanalala juu ya vitanda vilivyopambwa kwa pembe za ndovu \q na kustarehe juu ya makochi yao. \q Wanakula wana-kondoo kutoka kundini \q na ndama walionenepeshwa zizini.

decisions.choice: beds of ivory: furniture inlaid with carved ivory
decisions.reason: Panels of carved ivory were set into the frames of beds and couches for the very rich. Many such ivory pieces have been found in the ruins of Samaria. Amos has already named 'houses of ivory' (3:15; compare 1 Kings 22:39).

decisions.choice: calves from the midst of the stall: calves penned and fattened for the table
decisions.reason: Most people ate meat rarely, at feasts. These leaders eat lambs and stall-fattened calves as ordinary fare.

decisions.choice: sprawl: lounge at ease, stretched out
decisions.reason: Seruchim means hanging over or sprawling. The word returns in verse 7, where the 'sprawlers' go into exile.

decisions.choice: inlaid with (B), decorated with (R); fattened in the stall (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say how the beds were made of ivory (m1) and why the calves came from the stall (m2). Balanced and Readable begin new sentences with 'They'; the Hebrew runs on from verse 3 with 'those who'.

source.text: הַפֹּרְטִ֖ים עַל־פִּ֣י הַנָּ֑בֶל כְּדָוִ֕יד חָשְׁב֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם כְּלֵי־שִֽׁיר׃

records.literal_gloss: Those who improvise on [the] mouth of the harp; like David they have devised for themselves instruments of song.

en.L: who improvise to the sound of the harp; \q like David they devise for themselves instruments of song,
en.B: They improvise songs to the sound of the harp, \q and like David they invent musical instruments for themselves.
en.R: They make up songs as they play their harps. \q Like King David, they invent new musical instruments for themselves.

es.L: que improvisan al son del arpa; \q como David, inventan para sí instrumentos de música,
es.B: Improvisan canciones al son del arpa \q y, como David, se inventan instrumentos musicales.
es.R: Inventan canciones mientras tocan sus arpas. \q Como el rey David, se inventan nuevos instrumentos musicales.

fr.L: qui improvisent au son de la harpe ; \q comme David, ils s’inventent des instruments de musique,
fr.B: Ils improvisent des chants au son de la harpe, \q et, comme David, ils s’inventent des instruments de musique.
fr.R: Ils inventent des chansons en jouant de la harpe. \q Comme le roi David, ils s’inventent de nouveaux instruments de musique.

sw.L: wanaobuni nyimbo kwa sauti ya kinubi; \q kama Daudi wanajitungia vyombo vya nyimbo,
sw.B: Wanabuni nyimbo kwa sauti ya kinubi, \q na kama Daudi wanajitengenezea vyombo vya muziki.
sw.R: Wanatunga nyimbo wanapopiga vinubi vyao. \q Kama mfalme Daudi, wanajitengenezea vyombo vipya vya muziki.

decisions.choice: improvise: make up idle songs, strum carelessly
decisions.reason: Parat occurs only here. It seems to mean making up songs or strumming on a whim, the idle music of a drinking party.

decisions.choice: like David: David was remembered as a musician and the one who arranged the music of worship
alternatives: they think themselves like David with their musical instruments
decisions.reason: David played the lyre (1 Samuel 16:23), and later tradition says that he made instruments for the music of the temple (1 Chronicles 23:5; Nehemiah 12:36). The leaders spend the same skill on their own parties. The verb can also mean 'think', and some read the line as 'they think themselves like David with their instruments'.

decisions.choice: King David (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says who David was.

source.text: הַשֹּׁתִ֤ים בְּמִזְרְקֵי֙ יַ֔יִן וְרֵאשִׁ֥ית שְׁמָנִ֖ים יִמְשָׁ֑חוּ וְלֹ֥א נֶחְל֖וּ עַל־שֵׁ֥בֶר יוֹסֵֽף

records.literal_gloss: Those who drink in bowls of wine, and [with] the first of oils they anoint; and they are not sick over the ruin of Joseph.

en.L: who drink wine in bowls \q and anoint [themselves] with the finest of oils, \q but are not grieved over the ruin of Joseph!
en.B: They drink wine by the bowlful \q and anoint themselves with the finest oils, \q but they do not grieve over the ruin of Joseph.
en.R: They drink wine by the bowlful. \q They rub the best oils on their skin. \q But they do not care at all that Israel is falling apart.

es.L: que beben vino en tazones \q y se ungen con los mejores aceites, \q ¡pero no se afligen por la ruina de José!
es.B: Beben vino a tazones \q y se ungen con los aceites más finos, \q pero no se afligen por la ruina de José.
es.R: Beben vino a tazones. \q Se untan la piel con los mejores aceites. \q Pero no les importa nada que Israel se esté viniendo abajo.

fr.L: qui boivent le vin dans des coupes \q et s’oignent des meilleures huiles, \q mais ne s’affligent pas de la ruine de Joseph !
fr.B: Ils boivent le vin à pleines coupes \q et se parfument avec les huiles les plus fines, \q mais ils ne s’affligent pas de la ruine de Joseph.
fr.R: Ils boivent le vin à pleines coupes. \q Ils se frottent la peau avec les meilleures huiles. \q Mais cela leur est bien égal qu’Israël s’écroule.

sw.L: wanaokunywa divai katika mabakuli \q na kujipaka mafuta yaliyo bora kabisa, \q lakini hawahuzuniki kwa ajili ya maangamizi ya Yusufu!
sw.B: Wanakunywa divai kwa mabakuli \q na kujipaka mafuta bora kabisa, \q lakini hawahuzuniki kwa ajili ya maangamizi ya Yusufu.
sw.R: Wanakunywa divai kwa mabakuli. \q Wanajipaka mafuta bora kabisa mwilini. \q Lakini hawajali hata kidogo kwamba Israeli inaangamia.

decisions.choice: bowls: large basins, of the kind used in worship
decisions.reason: Mizraq is the word for the large bowls used to toss the blood of sacrifices at the altar (Exodus 27:3; Numbers 7:13). Drinking wine from such bowls shows excess, and perhaps contempt for holy things.

decisions.choice: anoint with the finest oils: rub fine oil on the skin, a luxury
decisions.reason: Oil rubbed on the skin and hair was a mark of comfort and festivity; it was left off in mourning (2 Samuel 14:2). 'The first of oils' repeats the word of verse 1: the leaders of 'the first of the nations' use 'the first of oils'.

decisions.choice: not grieved over the ruin of Joseph: unmoved by the collapse of their own people
decisions.reason: Shever is a break or fracture. Joseph stands for the northern kingdom (5:6, 15). The leaders do not grieve over the breaking of their own people, which has begun in the oppression of the poor and will end in exile.

decisions.choice: do not care at all that Israel is falling apart (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says 'Israel' for 'Joseph' (5:6) and 'falling apart' for 'ruin', the word for a break.

decisions.choice: "la ruina de José" (L, B); "Israel" (R)
decisions.reason: Joseph stands for the northern kingdom, as "la casa de José" in 5:6; R names Israel, as the English R does.

source.text: לָכֵ֛ן עַתָּ֥ה יִגְל֖וּ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ גֹּלִ֑ים וְסָ֖ר מִרְזַ֥ח סְרוּחִֽים׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Therefore now they will go into exile at [the] head of [the] exiles, and will pass away [the] revelry of [the] sprawlers.

en.L: Therefore now they will go into exile at the head of the exiles, \q and the revelry of those who sprawl will pass away.
en.B: So now they will be the first to go into exile, \q and the feasting of the loungers will come to an end.
en.R: So they will be the first to be taken away as captives. \q Their parties, where they lounge on couches, will be over.

es.L: Por tanto, ahora irán al destierro a la cabeza de los desterrados, \q y se acabará el banquete de los que se tienden.
es.B: Por eso ahora serán los primeros en ir al destierro, \q y se acabará el festín de los que se recuestan.
es.R: Por eso serán los primeros en ser llevados prisioneros. \q Se acabarán sus fiestas, en las que se recuestan en sus divanes.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi maintenant ils iront en exil à la tête des exilés, \q et la fête de ceux qui s’étalent prendra fin.
fr.B: Aussi, maintenant, ils seront les premiers à partir en exil, \q et les banquets de ces fainéants prendront fin.
fr.R: Alors ils seront les premiers à être emmenés en captivité. \q Leurs fêtes, où ils se prélassent sur des divans, seront finies.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo sasa watakwenda uhamishoni wakiwa mbele ya wanaohamishwa, \q na sherehe za wale wanaojinyoosha zitakoma.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo sasa watakuwa wa kwanza kwenda uhamishoni, \q na karamu za hao wanaostarehe zitakwisha.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo watakuwa wa kwanza kuchukuliwa mateka. \q Karamu zao, wanapostarehe juu ya makochi, zitakwisha.

decisions.choice: at the head of the exiles: first in line, as they are first in everything
decisions.reason: Rosh, 'head', echoes 'the first' of verses 1 and 6: those who think themselves first among the nations will lead the line of captives.

decisions.choice: revelry: the feast of a group of companions
decisions.reason: Marzeach is the name of a feast held by a group of companions, with much eating and drinking. Jeremiah 16:5 uses the word for a funeral meal. Here it is the drinking party of verses 4-6, and it is about to end.

source.text: נִשְׁבַּע֩ אֲדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֜ה בְּנַפְשׁ֗וֹ נְאֻם־יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י צְבָא֔וֹת מְתָאֵ֤ב אָֽנֹכִי֙ אֶת־גְּא֣וֹן יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וְאַרְמְנֹתָ֖יו שָׂנֵ֑אתִי וְהִסְגַּרְתִּ֖י עִ֥יר וּמְלֹאָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] Lord Yahweh has sworn by himself, declares Yahweh God of hosts: I loathe the pride of Jacob, and his fortresses I hate; and I will deliver up [the] city and its fullness.

en.L: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} has sworn by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of hosts: \q I loathe the pride of Jacob, \q and I hate his fortresses; \q and I will deliver up the city and all that fills it.
en.B: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} has sworn by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies: \q I detest the pride of Jacob \q and hate his fortresses; \q I will hand over the city and everything in it.
en.R: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} has sworn by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies: \q I hate the pride of Jacob's people, \q and I hate their fortresses. \q I will hand over their city and everything in it to the enemy.

es.L: El Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} ha jurado por {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}} mismo, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los ejércitos: \q Aborrezco la soberbia de Jacob, \q y odio sus fortalezas; \q y entregaré la ciudad y todo lo que la llena.
es.B: El Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} ha jurado por {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}} mismo, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los Ejércitos: \q Detesto el orgullo de Jacob \q y odio sus fortalezas; \q entregaré la ciudad con todo lo que hay en ella.
es.R: El Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} ha jurado por {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}} mismo, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los Ejércitos: \q Odio el orgullo del pueblo de Jacob, \q y odio sus fortalezas. \q Entregaré al enemigo su ciudad y todo lo que hay en ella.

fr.L: Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} l’a juré par {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des armées : \q J’ai en horreur l’orgueil de Jacob, \q et je hais ses forteresses ; \q et je livrerai la ville et tout ce qui la remplit.
fr.B: Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} l’a juré par {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des armées : \q Je déteste l’orgueil de Jacob \q et je hais ses forteresses ; \q je livrerai la ville et tout ce qu’elle contient.
fr.R: Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} l’a juré par {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des armées : \q Je déteste l’orgueil du peuple de Jacob, \q et je hais ses forteresses. \q Je livrerai à l’ennemi sa ville et tout ce qu’elle contient.

sw.L: Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} ameapa kwa nafsi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi: \q Nachukia kabisa kiburi cha Yakobo, \q na ngome zake nazichukia; \q nami nitautoa mji na vyote vilivyomo.
sw.B: Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} ameapa kwa nafsi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi: \q Nakichukia sana kiburi cha Yakobo \q na kuzichukia ngome zake; \q nitautia mji na kila kitu kilichomo mikononi mwa adui.
sw.R: Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} ameapa kwa nafsi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi: \q Nakichukia kiburi cha wazao wa Yakobo, \q na nazichukia ngome zao. \q Nitautia mji wao na kila kitu kilichomo mikononi mwa adui.

decisions.choice: sworn by himself: by his own life, with no one greater to swear by
decisions.reason: Nefesh is the self or the life. The LORD can swear by no one greater than himself (Genesis 22:16; Hebrews 6:13), so the oath cannot be broken. Amos records such oaths also in 4:2 (by his holiness) and 8:7.

decisions.choice: the pride of Jacob: the people's arrogant self-confidence
decisions.reason: Ge'on can mean majesty in a good sense, but here it is the pride that trusts in wealth and fortresses. In 8:7 the LORD swears 'by the pride of Jacob'.

decisions.choice: deliver up the city and all that fills it: give it up to the enemy, with its people and goods
decisions.reason: Hisgir means to hand over, to deliver to an enemy (Deuteronomy 32:30). 'The city' is probably Samaria (verse 1).

decisions.choice: declares the LORD God of hosts (L); declares the LORD God of Armies (B); says the LORD God of Armies (R)
decisions.reason: Ne'um YHWH is 'declares the LORD' at Literal and Balanced and 'says the LORD' at Readable, as in Isaiah, with the title as in 5:14. Readable says 'Jacob's people' and 'to the enemy' to make plain who is meant.

decisions.choice: "ha jurado por sí mismo"
decisions.reason: "Sí" is God's free pronoun here and takes the deity_pronoun span, as "Himself" in the English.

source.text: וְהָיָ֗ה אִם־יִוָּ֨תְר֜וּ עֲשָׂרָ֧ה אֲנָשִׁ֛ים בְּבַ֥יִת אֶחָ֖ד וָמֵֽתוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be, if there remain ten men in one house, they will die.

en.L: And it will be, if ten {{gender:people|men}} remain in one house, they will die.
en.B: If ten {{gender:people|men}} are left in one house, they too will die.
en.R: If ten {{gender:people|men}} are still alive in one house, they will all die.

es.L: Y sucederá que si quedan diez {{gender:personas|hombres}} en una casa, morirán.
es.B: Si quedan diez {{gender:personas|hombres}} en una casa, también morirán.
es.R: Si en una casa todavía quedan con vida diez {{gender:personas|hombres}}, morirán todos.

fr.L: Et il arrivera que, s’il reste dix {{gender:personnes|hommes}} dans une seule maison, ils mourront.
fr.B: S’il reste dix {{gender:personnes|hommes}} dans une maison, eux aussi mourront.
fr.R: Si dix {{gender:personnes|hommes}} sont encore vivants dans une maison, ils mourront tous.

sw.L: Na itakuwa, kama watu kumi wakibaki katika nyumba moja, watakufa.
sw.B: Kama watu kumi wakibaki katika nyumba moja, nao pia watakufa.
sw.R: Kama watu kumi bado wako hai katika nyumba moja, wote watakufa.

decisions.choice: ten in one house ... they will die: even those who survive the first blow will die
decisions.reason: Verses 9-10 picture the city after the disaster of verse 8. Ten people in one house was a large household; even they will die, until hardly anyone is left to bury the dead.

decisions.choice: men: people, men and women
decisions.reason: 'Anashim, the plural of 'ish, 'man', often means people in general. Here it is everyone left in the house.

decisions.choice: {{gender:personas|hombres}}
decisions.reason: Spanish has two wordings here, as the English does: "personas" for the men and women of the house, "hombres" for the Hebrew word.

decisions.choice: "dix {{gender:personnes|hommes}}"
decisions.reason: The word means people, men and women (the meaning decision); French "personnes" says so, with the traditional "hommes" as the alternative, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "watu kumi" with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Watu" covers men and women, as the meaning decision says, so Swahili has no second wording for the gender setting to choose.

source.text: וּנְשָׂא֞וֹ דּוֹד֣וֹ וּמְסָרְפ֗וֹ לְהוֹצִ֣יא עֲצָמִים֮ מִן־הַבַּיִת֒ וְאָמַ֞ר לַאֲשֶׁ֨ר בְּיַרְכְּתֵ֥י הַבַּ֛יִת הַע֥וֹד עִמָּ֖ךְ וְאָמַ֣ר אָ֑פֶס וְאָמַ֣ר הָ֔ס כִּ֛י לֹ֥א לְהַזְכִּ֖יר בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And his relative will lift him up, and the one who burns him, to bring out bones from the house, and he will say to [the one] who [is] in the innermost parts of the house, [Is there] still [anyone] with you? And he will say, None. And he will say, Hush! For [we must] not mention the name of Yahweh.

en.L: And [when] his relative, the one who burns him, lifts him up to bring the bones out of the house, \q and says to the one in the innermost part of the house, "Is anyone still with you?" and that one says, "No one," \q then he will say, "Hush! \q For the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} must not be mentioned."
en.B: When a relative who is to burn the dead comes to carry the bodies out of the house, \q he will call to someone hiding deep inside the house, "Is anyone else with you?" When the answer comes, "No," \q he will say, "Hush! \q We must not mention the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.R: A relative will come to take the dead bodies out of the house and burn them. \q He will call to someone hiding in a back room, "Is anyone else still alive in there with you?" The person will answer, "No." \q Then the relative will say, "Be quiet! \q We must not even say the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

es.L: Y [cuando] su pariente, el que lo ha de quemar, lo levante para sacar los huesos de la casa, \q y diga al que está en lo más recóndito de la casa: «¿Hay todavía [alguien] contigo?», y este diga: «Nadie», \q entonces dirá: «¡Calla! \q Porque no se debe mencionar el nombre {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}».
es.B: Cuando un pariente que ha de quemar a los muertos venga a sacar los cuerpos de la casa, \q llamará a alguien escondido en lo más profundo de la casa: «¿Hay alguien más contigo?». Cuando le respondan: «No», \q dirá: «¡Silencio! \q No debemos mencionar el nombre {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}».
es.R: Un pariente vendrá a sacar de la casa los cadáveres para quemarlos. \q Llamará a alguien escondido en un cuarto del fondo: «¿Queda alguien más con vida ahí contigo?». La persona responderá: «No». \q Entonces el pariente dirá: «¡Cállate! \q No debemos ni siquiera decir el nombre {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}».

fr.L: Et [quand] son parent, celui qui le brûle, le soulèvera pour faire sortir les os de la maison, \q et qu’il dira à celui qui est au fond de la maison : « Y a-t-il encore quelqu’un avec toi ? » et que celui-ci dira : « Personne », \q alors il dira : « Silence ! \q Car il ne faut pas mentionner le nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. »
fr.B: Quand un parent chargé de brûler les morts viendra emporter les corps hors de la maison, \q il appellera quelqu’un caché au fond de la maison : « Y a-t-il encore quelqu’un avec toi ? » Et quand on lui répondra : « Non », \q il dira : « Silence ! \q Il ne faut pas mentionner le nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. »
fr.R: Un parent viendra emporter les corps hors de la maison pour les brûler. \q Il appellera quelqu’un caché dans une pièce du fond : « Y a-t-il encore quelqu’un de vivant avec toi ? » La personne répondra : « Non. » \q Alors le parent dira : « Tais-toi ! \q Il ne faut même pas prononcer le nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. »

sw.L: Na [jamaa] yake, yule atakayemchoma, atakapomwinua ili kuitoa mifupa nje ya nyumba, \q na kumwambia yule aliye katika vyumba vya ndani kabisa vya nyumba, "Je, bado yuko mtu pamoja nawe?" naye akasema, "Hakuna," \q ndipo atasema, "Nyamaza! \q Kwa maana jina la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} lisitajwe."
sw.B: Ndugu wa marehemu, atakayeichoma miili, atakapokuja kuitoa maiti nje ya nyumba, \q atamwita mtu aliyejificha ndani kabisa ya nyumba, "Je, kuna mtu mwingine pamoja nawe?" Naye akijibu, "Hakuna," \q atasema, "Nyamaza! \q Hatupaswi kulitaja jina la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."
sw.R: Ndugu mmoja atakuja kuzitoa maiti nje ya nyumba na kuzichoma. \q Atamwita mtu aliyejificha katika chumba cha nyuma, "Je, kuna mtu mwingine aliye hai humo pamoja nawe?" Naye atajibu, "Hapana." \q Ndipo ndugu huyo atasema, "Nyamaza! \q Hatupaswi hata kulitamka jina la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."

decisions.choice: his relative: literally 'his uncle', a close kinsman responsible for the burial
decisions.reason: Dod is an uncle or close relative. It fell to the family to bury its dead. 'Bones' here means the dead body.

decisions.choice: the one who burns him: the one who burns the body, or who burns spices for the dead
alternatives: one who burns spices for the dead
decisions.reason: Mesarref means 'one who burns'. Israelites normally buried their dead, so if the word means burning the body, it shows how great the disaster is: the dead are so many, perhaps from plague, that they must be burned (compare 1 Samuel 31:12). Others take it of burning spices in honor of the dead (2 Chronicles 16:14; Jeremiah 34:5). The line is hard, and the exact sense is not certain.

decisions.choice: Hush! The name of the LORD must not be mentioned: for fear of calling down more of his anger
decisions.reason: The survivor is afraid that to speak the LORD's name, even in a prayer or an oath, would draw his attention and bring more judgment. The LORD who was ignored in good times has become a terror. Has, 'hush', returns in 8:3.

decisions.choice: the dead, the bodies (B, R); hiding (B, R); still alive (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say 'the dead' and 'bodies' for 'him' and 'bones', and say that the one in the inner room is hiding, which the scene implies. Readable adds 'still alive' to the question.

source.text: כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ מְצַוֶּ֔ה וְהִכָּ֛ה הַבַּ֥יִת הַגָּד֖וֹל רְסִיסִ֑ים וְהַבַּ֥יִת הַקָּטֹ֖ן בְּקִעִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: For look, Yahweh [is] commanding, and he will strike the great house [into] fragments and the small house [into] pieces.

en.L: For look, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is giving the command, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will strike the great house into fragments, \q and the small house into pieces.
en.B: For look, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives the command, \q and the great house will be broken into fragments, \q and the small house into splinters.
en.R: Listen! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is giving the command. \q Big houses and small houses alike will be smashed to pieces.

es.L: Porque he aquí, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} da la orden, \q y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} herirá la casa grande [haciéndola] pedazos, \q y la casa pequeña [haciéndola] añicos.
es.B: Porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} da la orden, \q y la casa grande quedará hecha pedazos, \q y la casa pequeña, hecha astillas.
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}! {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está dando la orden. \q Las casas grandes y las pequeñas quedarán hechas pedazos.

fr.L: Car voici, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} donne l’ordre, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} frappera la grande maison [pour la mettre] en morceaux, \q et la petite maison en débris.
fr.B: Car voici, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} donne l’ordre, \q et la grande maison sera brisée en morceaux, \q et la petite en éclats.
fr.R: Écoutez ! {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} donne l’ordre. \q Les grandes maisons comme les petites seront mises en pièces.

sw.L: Kwa maana tazama, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anatoa amri, \q naye ataipiga nyumba kubwa ivunjike vipande vipande, \q na nyumba ndogo iwe vipande.
sw.B: Kwa maana tazama, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anatoa amri, \q na nyumba kubwa itavunjwa vipande vipande, \q na nyumba ndogo kuwa vibanzi.
sw.R: Sikilizeni! {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anatoa amri. \q Nyumba kubwa na nyumba ndogo pia zitavunjwa vipande vipande.

decisions.choice: he will strike: the LORD himself, or whoever acts at his command
decisions.reason: The subject of the verb is not named. It may be the LORD, or the enemy he commands, or an earthquake (1:1). The point is that no house, great or small, will stand.

decisions.choice: the great house and the small house: every house, rich or poor
decisions.reason: The pair means all houses. The 'great house' may be the mansions of the rich (3:15) and the small one the homes of the poor; the whole people will share the ruin.

decisions.choice: will be broken (B); will be smashed (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave the one who strikes unnamed, as the Hebrew does (m1), by saying that the houses 'will be broken' or 'smashed'.

source.text: הַיְרֻצ֤וּן בַּסֶּ֨לַע֙ סוּסִ֔ים אִֽם־יַחֲר֖וֹשׁ בַּבְּקָרִ֑ים כִּֽי־הֲפַכְתֶּ֤ם לְרֹאשׁ֙ מִשְׁפָּ֔ט וּפְרִ֥י צְדָקָ֖ה לְלַעֲנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Do horses run on the crag? Or does one plow [it] with oxen? For you have turned into poison justice, and [the] fruit of righteousness into wormwood.

en.L: Do horses run on rock? \q Or does one plow [there] with oxen? \q Yet you have turned justice to poison, \q and the fruit of righteousness to wormwood.
en.B: Do horses gallop over rocky crags? \q Does anyone plow rock with oxen? \q Yet you have made justice into poison \q and the fruit of righteousness into bitter wormwood.
en.R: Can horses run on rocky cliffs? \q Can farmers plow rock with oxen? \q But you have turned justice into poison. \q You have made the fruit of what is right as bitter as wormwood.

es.L: ¿Corren los caballos por la peña? \q ¿Se ara [allí] con bueyes? \q Pues {{plural_you:ustedes han|vosotros habéis}} convertido el derecho en veneno, \q y el fruto de la justicia en ajenjo.
es.B: ¿Galopan los caballos sobre los peñascos? \q ¿Ara alguien la roca con bueyes? \q Sin embargo, {{plural_you:ustedes han|vosotros habéis}} convertido el derecho en veneno \q y el fruto de la justicia en amargo ajenjo.
es.R: ¿Pueden correr los caballos sobre las rocas? \q ¿Pueden los campesinos arar la roca con bueyes? \q Pero {{plural_you:ustedes han|vosotros habéis}} convertido la justicia en veneno. \q {{plural_you:Han hecho|Habéis hecho}} que el fruto de lo correcto sea amargo como el ajenjo.

fr.L: Les chevaux courent-ils sur le rocher ? \q Ou y laboure-t-on avec des bœufs ? \q Pourtant vous avez changé le droit en poison, \q et le fruit de la justice en absinthe.
fr.B: Les chevaux galopent-ils sur les rochers escarpés ? \q Laboure-t-on le rocher avec des bœufs ? \q Pourtant vous avez fait du droit un poison \q et du fruit de la justice une absinthe amère.
fr.R: Les chevaux peuvent-ils courir sur des rochers escarpés ? \q Les paysans peuvent-ils labourer le rocher avec des bœufs ? \q Mais vous avez changé la justice en poison. \q Vous avez rendu le fruit de ce qui est juste aussi amer que l’absinthe.

sw.L: Je, farasi hukimbia juu ya mwamba? \q Au mtu hulima [huko] kwa ng'ombe? \q Lakini ninyi mmeigeuza hukumu kuwa sumu, \q na tunda la haki kuwa pakanga.
sw.B: Je, farasi hukimbia mbio juu ya miamba? \q Je, mtu hulima mwamba kwa ng'ombe? \q Lakini ninyi mmeigeuza haki kuwa sumu \q na tunda la uadilifu kuwa pakanga chungu.
sw.R: Je, farasi wanaweza kukimbia juu ya miamba mikali? \q Je, wakulima wanaweza kulima mwamba kwa ng'ombe? \q Lakini ninyi mmeigeuza haki kuwa sumu. \q Mmelifanya tunda la uadilifu kuwa chungu kama pakanga.

decisions.choice: does one plow with oxen?: understood as 'plow there (on the rock) with oxen'
alternatives: Does one plow the sea with oxen? (dividing the letters as babbaqar yam)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads 'Does one plow with oxen?', which needs 'on the rock' carried over from the first line, since there is nothing strange about plowing with oxen. If the same letters are divided into two words, they read 'Does one plow the sea with an ox?', a picture as absurd as horses running on rocks. The change adds no letters and many accept it, but it is a change to the written text, and the Hebrew as it stands can be understood.

decisions.choice: justice into poison, righteousness into wormwood: the courts that should give life bring death
decisions.reason: As in 5:7, mishpat and tsedaqah are fair judgment and right dealing. To turn them into poison (rosh, a poisonous plant) and wormwood is as unnatural as horses on the rocks: it goes against the way the world is made.

decisions.choice: the fruit of what is right; as bitter as wormwood (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says 'what is right' for tsedaqah, as settled for Amos, and adds 'as bitter as' to show what wormwood is (5:7).

source.text: הַשְּׂמֵחִ֖ים לְלֹ֣א דָבָ֑ר הָאֹ֣מְרִ֔ים הֲל֣וֹא בְחָזְקֵ֔נוּ לָקַ֥חְנוּ לָ֖נוּ קַרְנָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: Those who rejoice over Lo-debar, who say, [Is it] not by our own strength [that] we have taken for ourselves Karnaim?

en.L: [You] who rejoice over Lo-debar, \q who say, "Was it not by our own strength \q that we took Karnaim for ourselves?"
en.B: You rejoice over Lo-debar \q and say, "Did we not capture Karnaim \q with our own strength?"
en.R: You are proud that you captured Lo-debar, a name that means Nothing. \q You boast, "We captured Karnaim, the town of Horns, \q and we did it in our own strength!"

es.L: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}}, que se {{plural_you:alegran|alegráis}} por Lodebar, \q que {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: «¿No [fue] con nuestra propia fuerza \q que nos apoderamos de Carnáyim?».
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes se alegran|Vosotros os alegráis}} por Lodebar \q y {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: «¿No conquistamos Carnáyim \q con nuestra propia fuerza?».
es.R: {{plural_you:Están|Estáis}} orgullosos de haber conquistado Lodebar, un nombre que significa “Nada”. \q {{plural_you:Presumen|Presumís}}: «Conquistamos Carnáyim, la ciudad de los Cuernos, \q ¡y lo hicimos con nuestras propias fuerzas!».

fr.L: [Vous] qui vous réjouissez de Lo-Debar, \q qui dites : « N’est-ce pas par notre propre force \q que nous avons pris pour nous Qarnaïm ? »
fr.B: Vous vous réjouissez de Lo-Debar \q et vous dites : « N’avons-nous pas pris Qarnaïm \q par notre propre force ? »
fr.R: Vous êtes fiers d’avoir pris Lo-Debar, un nom qui veut dire « Rien ». \q Vous vous vantez : « Nous avons pris Qarnaïm, la ville des Cornes, \q et nous l’avons fait par notre propre force ! »

sw.L: [Ninyi] mnaofurahia Lo-debari, \q mnaosema, "Je, si kwa nguvu zetu wenyewe \q tulijitwalia Karnaimu?"
sw.B: Mnafurahia Lo-debari \q na kusema, "Je, hatukuuteka Karnaimu \q kwa nguvu zetu wenyewe?"
sw.R: Mnajivuna kwamba mliuteka Lo-debari, jina lenye maana ya Si Kitu. \q Mnajisifu, "Tuliuteka Karnaimu, mji wa Pembe, \q nasi tulifanya hivyo kwa nguvu zetu wenyewe!"

decisions.choice: Lo-debar and Karnaim: towns east of the Jordan, with names that mean 'nothing' and 'horns'
decisions.reason: Lo-debar and Karnaim were towns in Gilead, east of the Jordan, which Israel seems to have won back from Aram under Jeroboam II (2 Kings 14:25, 28). Amos plays on their names. Lo-debar sounds like lo' davar, 'nothing': the leaders rejoice over a thing of nothing. Karnaim means 'a pair of horns', and horns are a picture of strength (Deuteronomy 33:17): they boast that by their own strength they have taken 'Strength'.

decisions.choice: Was it not by our own strength?: a boast that leaves God out
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer 'Yes, it was'. The leaders credit their victories to themselves; verse 14 answers that the LORD will raise up a nation against them.

decisions.choice: a name that means Nothing; the town of Horns (R)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the names in the text, since the verse makes no sense without it (m1). Literal and Balanced keep the names and give the meaning in a footnote.

decisions.choice: "Lodebar", "Carnáyim"; R explains both names
decisions.reason: Lo-debar as 2 Samuel 17:27 in Spanish; Karnaim in Spanish spelling. R says the meaning of the names in the text, as the English R does, with “ ” for the word explained, since the line also holds « ».

decisions.choice: "Lo-debari", "Karnaimu"; Readable "Si Kitu", "mji wa Pembe"
decisions.reason: Lo-debari as published (2 Samuel 9:4); Karnaimu is new, in the usual pattern. Readable gives the meanings in Swahili, as the English Readable does, so the joke can be heard.

source.text: כִּ֡י הִנְנִי֩ מֵקִ֨ים עֲלֵיכֶ֜ם בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל נְאֻם־יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י הַצְּבָא֖וֹת גּ֑וֹי וְלָחֲצ֥וּ אֶתְכֶ֛ם מִלְּב֥וֹא חֲמָ֖ת עַד־נַ֥חַל הָעֲרָבָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For look, I [am] raising up against you, house of Israel, declares Yahweh God of the hosts, a nation; and they will oppress you from Lebo-hamath to the brook of the Arabah.

en.L: For look, I am raising up against you a nation, house of Israel, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of hosts; \q and they will oppress you from Lebo-hamath as far as the Wadi of the Arabah.
en.B: For look, I am about to raise up a nation against you, house of Israel, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies, \q and they will oppress you from Lebo-hamath to the Wadi of the Arabah.
en.R: People of Israel, I am about to send a nation to attack you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies. \q They will crush you, from Lebo-hamath in the north to the Wadi of the Arabah in the south.

es.L: Porque he aquí, yo levanto contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} una nación, casa de Israel, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los ejércitos; \q y {{plural_you:los|os}} oprimirán desde Lebo-hamat hasta el torrente del Arabá.
es.B: Porque voy a levantar contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} una nación, casa de Israel, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los Ejércitos, \q y {{plural_you:los|os}} oprimirán desde Lebo-hamat hasta el torrente del Arabá.
es.R: Pueblo de Israel, voy a enviar una nación para que {{plural_you:los|os}} ataque, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los Ejércitos. \q {{plural_you:Los|Os}} aplastarán desde Lebo-hamat, en el norte, hasta el torrente del Arabá, en el sur.

fr.L: Car voici, je suscite contre vous une nation, maison d’Israël, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des armées ; \q et ils vous opprimeront depuis Lebo-Hamath jusqu’au torrent de l’Araba.
fr.B: Car je vais susciter contre vous une nation, maison d’Israël, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des armées, \q et elle vous opprimera depuis Lebo-Hamath jusqu’au torrent de l’Araba.
fr.R: Peuple d’Israël, je vais envoyer une nation pour vous attaquer, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des armées. \q Elle vous écrasera, depuis Lebo-Hamath au nord jusqu’au torrent de l’Araba au sud.

sw.L: Kwa maana tazama, ninainua juu yenu taifa, enyi nyumba ya Israeli, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi; \q nao watawaonea kutoka Lebo-hamathi mpaka kijito cha Araba.
sw.B: Kwa maana tazama, ninakaribia kuinua taifa dhidi yenu, enyi nyumba ya Israeli, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi, \q nao watawadhulumu kutoka Lebo-hamathi mpaka kijito cha Araba.
sw.R: Enyi watu wa Israeli, ninakaribia kutuma taifa kuwashambulia, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi. \q Watawaponda, kuanzia Lebo-hamathi upande wa kaskazini mpaka kijito cha Araba upande wa kusini.

decisions.choice: from Lebo-hamath to the Wadi of the Arabah: the whole land, from its northern border to the south
decisions.reason: Lebo-hamath, 'the entrance to Hamath', marked Israel's northern border (Numbers 34:8). The Wadi of the Arabah was in the south, near the Dead Sea. Jeroboam II had restored Israel's border 'from Lebo-hamath to the Sea of the Arabah' (2 Kings 14:25). The same borders will mark the reach of the enemy's oppression.

decisions.choice: a nation: Assyria, though it is not named
decisions.reason: Amos never names Assyria as the enemy, but it was Assyria that conquered the northern kingdom in 722 BC (2 Kings 17:5-6).

decisions.choice: declares the LORD God of hosts (L); of Armies (B); says (R); in the north ... in the south (R)
decisions.reason: The formula and title follow 6:8; the article in 'the God of the hosts' makes no difference in English. Readable adds 'in the north' and 'in the south' to show that the whole land is meant (m1).

decisions.choice: "Lebo-hamat", "el torrente del Arabá"
decisions.reason: As 2 Kings 14:25 and 1 Chronicles 13:5 in Spanish, where Jeroboam's border runs "desde Lebo-hamat hasta el mar del Arabá".
